subject: SLA template discussion — availability exception + scaled monthly remedy (Olive Solutions)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@olive-sol.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Olive Solutions Legal <legal@olive-sol.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template — availability threshold and monthly remedy for Olive Solutions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran through the internal risk review and have two items that drive us to request a deviation from your standard SLA template before procurement will sign:

1) Availability baseline — with our workload pattern (highly batched inference during nightly windows) the standard 99.9% monthly uptime target exposes us to spurious credit triggers that don't reflect user-visible outages. We would like to request a baseline of 99.7% for the first 12 months (pilot), or alternatively a hard carveout that excludes nightly batch windows from availability calculations.

2) Monthly remedy cap — we need a more predictable cap for monthly service credits. Our procurement team is asking for a softened top band (e.g., smaller % credits for the largest outage band) and a guaranteed monthly ceiling to avoid bill volatility.

If you can share a short proposal that shows: a) proposed baseline, b) revised credit bands with examples of how a sample month would be calculated, and c) any operational carveouts (batch windows / maintenance), that would help speed internal approval.

We also need SOC 2 evidence and an audit contact to hand to our security team.

Attached: procurement checklist (we'll send the formal PO once SLA is aligned).

Best,

Samir Patel
Head of Procurement, Olive Solutions
procurement@olive-sol.com
[Attachment: procurement_checklist.pdf (pdf)]
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@olive-sol.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template — availability threshold and monthly remedy for Olive Solutions

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask and context. I looped in Marissa (account lead) and Karthik (product) so we can propose a concrete amendment.

High level proposal (attached as SLA_Proposal_OliveSolutions_v2.pdf):
- Baseline: keep 99.9% as the contractual baseline, but add an operational carveout that excludes scheduled batch windows up to 8 hours/month from availability calculations if they are pre-declared and configured with the Redwood routing policy.
- Measurement: availability will be measured on a rolling calendar month excluding any declared batch windows and agreed maintenance.
- Remedy bands (monthly credit schedule):
  • 99.9% - 99.5% = 10% of monthly service fee
  • 99.5% - 99.0% = 25% of monthly service fee
  • <99.0% = 40% of monthly service fee, with a hard cap at 50% for the month
- Pilot option: if Olive prefers a fixed baseline of 99.7% for 12 months, we can draft a pilot amendment that reduces the top band by 5% (so the worst-case credit is 35%) and include a quarterly review to revert to standard terms or continue.

Operational notes:
- We will provide SOC 2 Type II report and a named audit contact (security@redwood.com).
- DocuSign-ready amendment and a HubSpot record are attached for reference (HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/OS-7890).

Could you confirm whether Olive would prefer the carveout approach (keep 99.9% + carveouts) or the 12-month 99.7% pilot? Once you confirm, Marissa will produce an amendment and route to legal.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
[Attachment: SLA_Proposal_OliveSolutions_v2.pdf (pdf)]
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@olive-sol.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Olive Solutions Legal <legal@olive-sol.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template — availability threshold and monthly remedy for Olive Solutions

Evelyn — appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed bands. We've reviewed the attachment with our procurement team and legal. A couple of counterpoints:

- Carveout vs. pilot: procurement prefers a defined baseline (less subjective) for contract simplicity. We're proposing a 99.7% baseline for an initial 6-month pilot rather than 12 months, with the following modified remedy schedule for predictability:
  • 99.7% - 99.3% = 8% credit
  • 99.3% - 98.8% = 20% credit
  • <98.8% = 35% credit, with a monthly ceiling of 30% of the invoice for the pilot period

- We will require a review milestone at month 3 (operations + product) to validate measurement windows and adjust if the day/night split materially changes production impact.

- SOC 2 evidence is required before countersign; please send the latest report and the audit contact. Also include a short note describing how Redwood measures availability (metric definitions, what is considered downtime for these endpoints).

Attached: provisional mutual action plan (Olive_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx). If you can produce a clean amendment reflecting the 6-month 99.7% pilot and the concrete monthly ceilings, we can move to signatures quickly.

Thanks,

Samir Patel
Head of Procurement, Olive Solutions
[Attachment: Olive_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template — availability threshold and monthly remedy for Olive Solutions

Samir / Olive team — thanks for the counterproposal and the MAP. Quick summary and next steps from Redwood: 

Summary of agreed pilot terms (draft):
- Pilot baseline: 99.7% for 6 months starting on go-live date.
- Remedy bands during pilot (monthly):
  • 99.7% - 99.3% = 8% credit
  • 99.3% - 98.8% = 20% credit
  • <98.8% = 35% credit; however, Redwood will cap the pilot-month remedy at 30% of that month’s invoice (as a commercial concession).
- Measurement: Redwood will provide a measurement appendix describing the availability calculation, prefix/KV caveats, and how scheduled batch windows (must be pre-declared in writing) are excluded from the rolling calendar month.
- Review milestone: formal operations review at month 3 with both teams; results may trigger a rebaseline conversation.
- Deliverables before countersign: SOC 2 Type II report, audit contact, and the final DocuSign amendment.

I've prepared the DocuSign envelope and a clean amendment draft (link below). If Olive confirms acceptance of the pilot structure above, we'll populate the document, attach the SOC 2 report, and send for signatures.
